Class.summary: Controller responsible for managing the lifecycle of support tickets.
Class.remarks: Provides endpoints for creating, querying, updating, assigning, and transitioning support tickets. Enforces strict role-based data isolation: Admin: Unrestricted global visibility and administrative control. SupportAgent: Scoped strictly to assigned tickets. Customer: Scoped strictly to tickets they created. All error responses follow the RFC 7807 ProblemDetails specification.

Constructor.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
Constructor.param: The MediatR mediator instance used for dispatching queries and commands.
The service used to resolve authenticated user identity, ID, and role from JWT claims.

GetTickets.summary: Retrieves a paginated and filterable list of support tickets.
GetTickets.remarks: Ticket visibility is automatically filtered based on the caller's role: Admin: Can view all tickets in the system. SupportAgent: Can only view tickets assigned to them. Customer: Can only view tickets they personally submitted. Filtering & Search: Supports filtering by Status (Open, InProgress, Resolved, Closed), Priority (Low, Medium, High, Critical), and a case-insensitive substring search across ticket titles and descriptions. Sorting: Supports sorting by CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, Priority, or Status in Ascending or Descending order. Pagination: Page must be >= 1 (defaults to 1); PageSize must be between 1 and 100 (defaults to 10).
GetTickets.param: The query parameters including filtering, sorting, and pagination options.
GetTickets.returns: A paginated response containing ticket summary records, total item count, and pagination metadata.
GetTickets.response: Returns the paginated list of tickets matching the specified filters.
If query parameters fail validation (e.g., page < 1, pageSize outside 1..100, or invalid enum value).
If the request lacks a valid Bearer token or the token has expired.

GetTicketById.summary: Retrieves a single support ticket by its unique identifier.
GetTicketById.remarks: Access is enforced with IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) prevention: Admin: Authorized to view any ticket. SupportAgent: Authorized only if assigned to this ticket. Customer: Authorized only if they created this ticket. If the ticket does not exist or the caller lacks permission, a 404 Not Found is returned to prevent resource enumeration.
GetTicketById.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
GetTicketById.returns: The detailed ticket information including customer and assigned agent display names, timestamps, and current state.
GetTicketById.response: If the provided ticket ID is not a valid GUID format.
If the request lacks a valid Bearer token.
If the ticket was not found or the caller is not authorized to access it.

CreateTicket.summary: Submits and creates a new support ticket.
CreateTicket.remarks: Restricted to users in the Customer role. The creator ID is automatically extracted from authenticated JWT claims. Initial status is automatically set to Open. A Created activity event is recorded in the ticket audit trail. The response includes a Location header pointing to the newly created resource URI.
CreateTicket.param: The creation payload containing title (max 200 chars), description (max 4000 chars), and requested priority.
CreateTicket.returns: The newly created ticket response with generated ID and timestamps.
CreateTicket.response: The ticket was created successfully. The response body contains the ticket and the Location header has the resource URI.
If the payload fails validation (e.g., missing title, description exceeding 4000 characters, invalid priority enum).
If the user is not authenticated.
If the authenticated user does not have the Customer role.

UpdateTicket.summary: Updates the core content (Title and Description) of an existing ticket.
UpdateTicket.remarks: Restricted exclusively to users in the Admin role. Updates the ticket's Title, Description, and refreshes the UpdatedAt timestamp.
UpdateTicket.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket to update.
The update payload containing the new title (max 200 chars) and description (max 4000 chars).
UpdateTicket.response: If the update payload fails validation.
If the user is not authenticated.
If the caller does not have the Admin role.
If the ticket with the specified ID does not exist.

UpdateTicketStatus.summary: Transitions a ticket to a new status according to business state machine rules.
UpdateTicketStatus.remarks: Allowed status transitions are governed by both state machine and role permissions: Admin: Can transition to any valid status (Open, InProgress, Resolved, Closed). SupportAgent: Can transition assigned tickets between Open, InProgress, and Resolved. Support agents cannot close tickets. Customer: Can close their own tickets (Closed) or reopen a closed ticket (Open). Cannot set InProgress or Resolved. State Machine Invariants: An Open ticket cannot be directly resolved; it must move to InProgress first. A Closed ticket can only be transitioned back to Open (reopened). Automatically logs a StatusChanged or Closed activity event with previous and new status values.
UpdateTicketStatus.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
The status payload containing the target status enum value.
UpdateTicketStatus.response: The status was updated and an activity audit entry was recorded.
If the transition violates role permissions or state machine rules.
If the user is not authenticated.
If the ticket does not exist or the caller lacks permission to access it.

UpdateTicketPriority.summary: Updates the priority level of an existing ticket.
UpdateTicketPriority.remarks: Restricted exclusively to users in the Admin role. Valid priorities: Low (0), Medium (1), High (2), Critical (3). Automatically logs a PriorityChanged activity event with previous and new priority values.
UpdateTicketPriority.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
The priority payload containing the new priority enum value.
UpdateTicketPriority.response: If the provided priority value is not a valid enum value.
If the user is not authenticated.
If the caller does not have the Admin role.
If the ticket with the specified ID does not exist.

AssignAgent.summary: Assigns or reassigns a Support Agent to a ticket.
AssignAgent.remarks: Restricted exclusively to users in the Admin role. The specified agent must exist and have the SupportAgent role. Tickets in a Closed state cannot be assigned to an agent. An AgentAssigned activity event is automatically recorded in the ticket timeline.
AssignAgent.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the ticket.
The assignment payload containing the Support Agent's unique GUID.
AssignAgent.response: The agent was assigned successfully and the audit log was updated.
If the ticket is closed or the assigned user is not a Support Agent.
If the user is not authenticated.
If the caller does not have the Admin role.
If the ticket or the specified agent does not exist.
